title: Order at a café
goal: Ask clearly, then repair a misunderstanding.

options: Un café con leche, por favor.
why: A direct, polite order tells the worker what to make.
Yes, thank you sounds polite, but it does not answer what you want.
turns.repair: Quisiera un café con leche, por favor.

why: By card is useful later, but the worker is asking about size now.
You answered the size question with the size.
You have finished the order naturally.
Yes, please can suggest you want something else, when you are trying to finish the order.

title: Meet someone new
goal: Introduce yourself and keep a conversation moving.

why: This would fit a question about where you are from, not what your name is.
You give a name and invite theirs; replace Alex with your own name when practicing.

turns.meaning: Nice to meet you. Where are you from?
options: Vivo en Nueva York desde hace dos años.
why: Soy de introduces where you're from.
That describes where you live and for how long. It might be useful later but does not directly answer where you are from.

turns.meaning: And what do you like to do?
why: That would answer how you are, not what you like doing.
You give two activities; swap in your own interests in real life.

title: Shop at a market
goal: Ask a price and confirm the amount.

turns.meaning: Good morning. What are you looking for?
why: You name the item and quantity.
You named the fruit, but asked for two rather than the three you planned to buy.

turns.meaning: Yes. How many would you like?
why: That gives a price instead of answering how many you want.
A short answer is completely natural after the question.

turns.meaning: That's four dollars. Is that okay?
why: You confirm the price and close the purchase.
Asking the unit price can help, but the vendor is confirming the total of four dollars right now.

title: Ask for directions
goal: Get one usable direction, even if they speak quickly.

why: You answer with where you are going, but not which help you need.
You answer yes and ask for the subway.

turns.heard: Sigue derecho y gira a la izquierda.
why: Checking 'left, right?' verifies the crucial direction.
This is polite, but does not verify the left turn you need to remember.
This says you know the neighborhood; it does not acknowledge the directions.
You've understood and thanked them naturally.

title: Confirm an appointment
goal: Verify the day, time and your name.

turns.meaning: Good morning. Do you have an appointment?
options: Sí, tengo una cita a las tres.
Sí, estoy aquí para una visita.
why: You confirm you have an appointment at three.
You identify the purpose but do not confirm the appointment time.
That confirms an appointment but still does not supply the booking name requested.
A nombre de gives the booking name. Say your actual name instead.
turns.repair: La cita está a mi nombre.

why: You politely acknowledge the wait.
This asks for an appointment when you already have one and are being asked to wait.

title: Chat with a neighbor
goal: Describe your day and ask a follow-up.

options: Bien, un poco ocupado. ¿Y el tuyo?
why: That is an acceptable answer, but the stronger choice also invites the neighbor into the conversation.
You describe your day and return the question.

turns.meaning: Good too. Do you have plans this afternoon?
options: Sí, voy a cocinar en casa.
why: You explain a plausible plan; use your own activity in real life.
This is a valid answer if you have not planned anything, but it is less useful for practicing a specific activity.
That changes the goodbye to a promise about tomorrow rather than simply responding to see you later.
A natural and friendly goodbye.

title: Handle a restaurant mix-up
goal: Correct an order politely without losing the conversation.

why: You politely flag the mismatch and name the item you ordered.
Accepting the salad without mentioning the mismatch will not get the soup you ordered.
turns.repair: Perdón, creo que hubo un error.

why: That switches to salad instead of confirming the vegetable soup you originally wanted.
You confirm the corrected order clearly.
You acknowledge the help and finish politely.
The price question is possible, but it interrupts the server who has already agreed to bring the corrected dish.

title: Make plans with a friend
goal: Ask, negotiate a time and confirm the plan.

turns.meaning: Do you want to get coffee tomorrow?
why: You accept and say goodbye, but have not pinned down a time yet.
You agree and ask the next useful question.

options: Sí, a las nueve está bien.
why: You propose a different hour politely.
That accepts nine instead of negotiating the later time you prefer.

turns.heard: Sí, a las diez está perfecto.
why: You sound friendly, but confirming tomorrow is clearer than an unspecified later chat.
You confirm the plan and say goodbye.
